title: Death and life, to test
hookLine: He created death and life to test which of you is best in deed (67:2)

lines: THE VERSE SAYS DEATH AND LIFE.
cards: Say it out loud: life and death. That's the usual order in English. Birth first, then the end, like a biography, a gravestone, a hospital chart.
Now read the second verse of al-Mulk, and something is backwards. The Qur'an says Allah created death and life. Death first.
It's not a slip. And in the same breath it tells you why both were made, and the answer isn't about how much you do.

teach.b: Al-Mulk, verse two, in Pickthall: "Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving." Pickthall turns it into the familiar order.

The Arabic says al-mawt wa al-hayah: death, then life. Commentators offered reasons. Some say death is named first because it's the thing people forget, and remembering it changes how life gets lived.
Others say every person was lifeless, nothing, before they were given life. The Qur'an doesn't say which; it just puts death in front. Then the purpose: to test you, which of you is ahsanu 'amalan.
Best in deed. Not most in deed. Not the longest list, the busiest calendar, the most prayers stacked up.

teach.h: BEST IN DEED, NOT MOST IN DEED.
teach.b: An early ascetic who settled in Mecca, al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, is reported to have explained best as the most sincere and the most correct: done for Allah, and done the right way.
One without the other isn't best.
The verse closes with two names together: the Mighty, the Forgiving. The test is real, and so is the mercy. The one who sets it can't be fooled, and also forgives.
Put the verse on an ordinary day. You don't have to do everything. Death comes for everyone, so the question isn't how much time is left.
It's what one thing, done today, could be done well, and for the right reason.

how: Muslims often cite 67:2 to say that what matters before Allah is the quality of a deed, done sincerely and correctly, rather than its quantity; it is also read nightly by those who keep the habit of reciting al-Mulk.

o: most in deed: the longest list of works
a good deed done to be seen by others
best in deed: most sincere, most correct

games.q: death and life — tap the pairs.

s: the Arabic of 67:2 names life before death
it says al-mawt wa al-hayah: death, then life.
the test is which of you does the most deeds
it's which is best in deed, ahsanu 'amalan.
the verse ends naming Allah the Mighty and the Forgiving
the test is real, and so is the mercy.

games.q: you have one free hour and a long list of good things you could do. by 67:2, what does the test look at?
games.why: best in deed, not most. al-Fudayl is reported to have said: the most sincere and the most correct.

practice: Look at today's list, the real one in your head, and pick one ordinary item: a meal, a reply, a chore, a prayer. Ask two questions: why am I doing it, and how would it look done well?
Picture doing it that way, start to finish, with nothing rushed.

wordCard.voice: Ahsanu 'amalan. Best in deed, not most: in 67:2 Allah creates death, then life, to test which of you is most sincere and most correct. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, 67:2: best in deed. ahsan, best, most excellent; 'amal, deed, work.

carryVoice: Your line: best in deed. The week ran from small and steady, through kindness, a way out, turning back and a house near you, to the surah before sleep. Another week behind you.

sources.q: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving.

sources.ref: saying of al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad on ahsanu 'amalan, reported in classical tafsir (e.g. al-Baghawi, Ibn Kathir)
